newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sister of Mexico's Salinas denies drug mansion.
newsitem.headline: Sister of Mexico's Salinas denies drug mansion.

text.p: Former Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari's sister on Friday denied receiving a seaside mansion from an agent of a Colombian cocaine king.
Mexican radio station Radio Red said on Thursday that federal agents were investigating possible links between the former first family and Colombia's Medellin cartel headed by Pablo Escobar.

Prosecutors could not confirm the report, the latest in a series of Mexican press allegations about connections between traffickers and members of the Salinas family. The family have strongly denied all the accusations, saying they are part of a coordinated smear campaign.

Radio Red said Adriana Salinas de Gortari had met a Colombian cartel go-between, named as Fanny de la Barrera, in New York in February 1994 and received from her the deeds to a huge, partly built mansion valued at more than $2 million in Punta Piedra, along the Caribbean coast from the resort of Cancun.
Construction of the 11-room mansion with 500 yards (metres) of private beach was abandoned after police shot Escobar to death on a Medellin rooftop in December 1993, the radio said.

Adriana Salinas de Gortari said in a handwritten statement faxed to Reuters that she did not own any property in the Cancun area or remember ever having met de la Barrera "and far less have any relationship whatsoever with her." She was not even in New York in February 1994, she added.
"This is another slander, sown by Pablo Chapa Bezanilla and Antonio Lozano Gracia to defame me and my family," Salinas said.

She was referring to former Mexican Attorney-General Antonio Lozano, who ordered the arrest of her brother Raul in March 1995 on charges of illicit enrichment and conspiracy to murder, and Pablo Chapa, who was a chief prosecutor handling, among other things, the murder case against Raul Salinsas.

Both men were fired by President Ernesto Zedillo in December for alleged incompetence and authorities are now seeking Chapa's arrest after the discovery of faked evidence and bribed witnesses in the case.
